title: Standardize enterprise request scoring and SLA-aware advisory pipeline for optimization asks
creator: Anika Shah
description:
Background: We have an increasing number of enterprise customers requesting tailored optimization advisory (batching/caching knobs, quantization profiles, routing policy recommendations). Current intake is ad-hoc via support tickets and sales handoffs which leads to slow turnaround, inconsistent recommendations, and missed SLAs for high-value accounts.

Goals: 
- Create a repeatable intake + scoring rubric that prioritizes requests by customer impact, security/regulatory constraints, and technical feasibility.
- Route requests automatically to the appropriate queue (self-serve docs, advisory team, dedicated engineering spot, or Partner Solutions) based on SLA tier.
- Provide a consistent deliverable: advisory note with suggested config changes, estimated cost delta, test plan, and runbooks for ops.
- Integrate advisory outcomes into Console (advisory history per customer) and the ticketing system for traceability.

Scope: 
- Intake form + minimal metadata capture (workload type, peak QPS, latency target, current model & variant, data sensitivity, customer tier).
- Scoring rubric and routing policy for P0/P1/P2 classification.
- Advisory template and acceptance criteria.
- Dashboard for triage metrics and SLA tracking.

Non-goals: 
- Building automated quantization tooling — this ticket covers advisory and human-led recommendations only.
- Immediate autoscaling policy changes in Dedicated. Those will be separate ENG work items.

Success metrics: 
- Triage SLAs met for P0/P1 requests (time-to-first-response 24h for P0, 72h for P1).
- Reduction in advisory turnaround time by 40% vs baseline.
- >80% advisory recommendations marked "actionable" by customers after 30 days.

Stakeholders: 
- Product (PM): Anika Shah (owner)
- Advisory ops: Liam Ortega (assignee)
- Serving runtime Eng leads: Priya Menon, Mateo Ruiz
- Solutions & Sales engineering: Tanya Reed
- Security & Compliance: Jordan Blake

Proposed approach: 
1) Intake form (Zendesk + Console link): short structured form that captures key signals for scoring. Minimal fields to avoid friction.
2) Scoring rubric: weighted scores (customer ARR / revenue weight 30%, latency/availability requirement weight 25%, data sensitivity 20%, technical complexity 15%, opportunity for productization 10%). Pre-define thresholds for P0/P1/P2.
3) SLA-aware routing: map score buckets to queues and SLAs. P0 -> Immediate advisory on-call; P1 -> advisory queue with 72h TTR; P2 -> self-serve content + watchlist.
4) Advisory deliverable template: executive summary, recommended knobs (batch size, KV cache hints, cache TTLs), quantization tradeoffs (accuracy delta / cost savings estimate), routing policy suggestions, rollback plan, and a test checklist.
5) Feedback loop: post-advisory survey that feeds a quality metric used in future scoring and to inform Optimize product features.

Trade-offs and open questions: 
- Simplicity vs accuracy in scoring: a simple rubric speeds triage but may misclassify edge cases. We'll start simple and iterate.
- Automation vs human review: full automation risks inappropriate advice for regulated customers; plan: automate routing decisions but require manual approval for "sensitive" flagged requests.
- Data needed for scoring (ARR): Sales may not provide clean ARR info for all accounts. Fallback: account tier + recent usage as proxy.

Risks: 
- Underestimating engineering capacity for advisory follow-ups; mitigation: reserve buffer capacity and define escalation to Dedicated contracts.
- Security/regulatory misclassification; mitigation: add required flag preventing automated advice for flagged industries.

Deliverables: 
- Intake form + Zendesk trigger + Console quick-link.
- Scoring document and config (stored in Confluence).
- Advisory template and sample advisory for two pilot customers.
- Triage dashboard prototype (Grafana/Console).

Next steps (this ticket): 
- Finalize scoring weights with Sales & Security (this week).
- Build intake form and add to support flows (ENG + CS).
- Pilot with 3 enterprise customers and iterate.
